body.summary: vscode-plugin/src/chat/chat-panel.ts renderShell, only when deps.queue is set (queueOn): #insrc-outbox (summary #insrc-obsum, rows #insrc-oblist, note #insrc-obnote) sits above the .inputbar; #insrc-qhint '⌘/Ctrl+Enter to queue' sits beside #insrc-input. Styles use the chat's theme variables only (no literals): rounded rows, round icon-only buttons (.outbox__btn, border-radius 50%) per the plugin UI convention. The script's renderOutbox(view) ignores another chat's view, builds the summary ('N messages from other chats ahead · running: “title” (this window) · waiting for an approval/a choice in “title”'), and draws each row with textContent: place '#n' or the state ('failed' / 'not sent'), the first line (full text in the title tooltip), the attachment count, the error, then ✕ cancel for queued/retrying or ↻ resend + ✕ dismiss for failed/not-delivered; each button has role=button, tabindex 0, aria-label and title, and posts its outbox-* type with the seq on click or Enter/Space. The band hides when there is nothing to show. setRunning toggles the hint; with the queue, doSubmit no longer calls setRunning(true)/setProgress (the host's 'turn-running' does); without the queue doSubmit is byte-identical, so the pinned tests (chat-panel.test.ts:1622, :1683, chat-shell.test.ts:334) stand. Test: the named test in chat-shell.test.ts runs the real script on the fake DOM (runShell gains a queue option with an inert worker). Mutations (marking running on submit with the queue, a hint that never hides, drawing another chat's outbox, a band that never hides) each fail it. Plugin suite: 1302 tests, 1292 pass, 8 skipped, 2 fail (pre-existing manifest-catalog). Typecheck clean.
